candidates.title: Schneider to shift eastern rail business to Norfolk Southern from CSX
candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. The companies said the partnership would expand market access, increase capacity flexibility and help attract freight now moving by truck. “As we transition our primary eastern rail provider to Norfolk Southern, we’ll expand access to key markets, increase network flexibility and create new opportunities to better serve our customers,” said Michael Baumgardt, Schneider’s executive vice president of intermodal and logistics, in a release. candidates.title: Track defect led to 2025 CN derailment in Mississippi: NTSB
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — A defect in a curve — which Canadian National did not properly address — led to the July 5, 2025, derailment and hazardous-materials release in Glendora, Miss., the National Transportation Safety Board said in an investigation report released today (Oct. 29). The 22-car derailment led to the breach of a tank car carrying benzene, which caught fire, requiring evacuation of about 160 people in a 1-mile radius [see “CN derailment in Mississippi …,” Trains.com, July 5, 2025]. No one was injured. CN estimated damages to be about $1.5 million. The southbound train with two locomotives and 139 cars was traveling at 29 mph at 2:26 p.m. when a train-initiated emergency brake application occurred near milepost 97.63 on CN’s Yazoo Subdivision. The train’s crew found that cars 29 through 50 had derailed, with one car on fire. The fire was extinguished about 11:30 p.m., and the evacuation order was lifted shortly thereafter. candidates.title: Ghislain Houle, CN chief financial officer, to retire
candidates.excerpt: MONTREAL — Ghislain Houle, Canadian National’s chief financial officer, will retire early in 2027, and will be succeeded by Jamie Lockwood, currently vice president, investor relations and special projects. The company announced the move today (Thursday, Oct. 29) ahead of its quarterly earnings call on Friday. Houle will remain CFO through Jan. 31, 2027, which the railroad says will ensure continuity through the year-end reporting cycle. He will then serve as strategic advisor to CEO Tracy Robinson through March 31, 2027, when he will retire. Lockwood will become executive vice president and CFO on Feb. 1, 2027. Houle has spent more than three decades at CN, holding progressively senior leadership roles. candidates.title: 9 alleged Mexican Cartel associates arrested in California train theft ring
candidates.excerpt: Nine men allegedly connected to Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel have been arrested in Southern California following a yearlong investigation into an organized cargo theft operation that targeted BNSF Railway trains and resulted in millions of dollars in stolen merchandise, authorities said. The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department announced Wednesday that its Rural Crime Task Force arrested the nine suspects Oct. 16 during a search of a residence in San Bernardino. Investigators said the suspects were part of a coordinated criminal network connected to the Sinaloa Cartel that had been burglarizing BNSF Railway trains over the past 12 months. The investigation uncovered an operation involving numerous suspects and vehicles used to steal merchandise from rail shipments, according to the Sheriff’s Department. candidates.title: Trinity reports higher railcar orders, tightening leasing market
candidates.excerpt: DALLAS — New freight car deliveries will bottom out this year, Trinity Industries executives said today while announcing third-quarter financial results. “In Rail Products, deliveries increased 29% sequentially and orders exceeded deliveries … A shrinking fleet and fewer railcars in storage point to a tightening market, and we believe 2026 will mark the cyclical low point for industry deliveries,” CEO Jean Savage said. October marked the 17th straight month that the North American freight car fleet shrank. Eighteen percent of freight cars were in storage, Trinity said, which is the lowest reading since May 2023. “This year, we’re talking about 40,000 cars being scrapped and less than 25,000 new cars being built. So the market is staying very tight overall,” Savage said on the company’s earnings call. candidates.title: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure
candidates.excerpt: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure Non-bank lenders are charging increasingly higher margins on complex net asset value (NAV) facilities despite wider pricing compression across the fund finance market, according to a new report from Corpay Private Markets. The fifth edition of the firm’s Lender Book Report found that average non-bank NAV lending margins widened from 756 basis points in February 2025 to 794 basis points in August 2026. By contrast, average bank NAV margins narrowed from 447 to 435 basis points over the same period. This comes as the fund finance lender base continues to diversify, with alternative credit providers accounting for around 30 per cent of lenders tracked by Corpay’s Alpha Match platform, up from roughly 25 per cent three years ago. candidates.excerpt: CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering expects profit surge Container ship newbuild deals drive the company’s hitting 217% of its annual order target in nine months CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering has forecast a notable jump in profits for the first nine months of 2026. The company projects its net profit attributable to owners of the parent for the January–September period to be between RMB1.10 billion and RMB 1.25 billion, a year-on-year increase of RMB 444.88 million to RMB 594.88 million, or a growth rate ranging from 67.91% to 90.80%. Its net profit attributable to parent owners is expected to hit RMB1 billion to RMB1.15 billion over the same timeframe, rising RMB 394.89 million to RMB 544.89 million from the 2025 comparable period, up 65.26% to 90.05% year on year. The strong expected performance stems from buoyant market conditions across the shipbuilding sector and solid operational execution by the firm.
